results.output: The on-premises AI box does not meet the firm’s requirements for reliable, high-quality document production at scale. The model’s send-readiness score remains at 3.00, significantly below the frontier cloud model’s 4.37, and fine-tuning failed to close this gap despite training on the device itself. The hardware supports only one user at full speed, meaning performance degrades under concurrent use and a second unit would be needed for consistent throughput. Additionally, the model occasionally generates unsupported details during open-ended drafting, requiring mandatory human review of all client-facing output. Despite these shortcomings, the box delivers strong throughput for its class, achieving 92.28 tokens per second on a mixture-of-experts model and 28x real-time transcription with Whisper. Document accuracy in summarisation tasks reached 93%, and tool use was correct in 91% of cases with no malformed calls. The device enables full local fine-tuning without cloud dependency, a benefit for data control. However, the limitations in output quality, scalability, and reliability outweigh these advantages for a firm that demands consistent, professional-grade results.

The model’s output, even after adaptation using a LoRA adapter trained directly on the device, remains at a send-readiness score of 3.00—well below the frontier cloud model’s 4.37. The fine-tune delivered only marginal improvements in tone (+0.3 to +0.5) and usability (+0.1 to +0.2), both within the margin of run-to-run variability. This confirms that the hardware does not support quality enhancement through training alone. The box also cannot sustain performance across multiple users. At full speed, it serves only one user at a time; concurrent demand results in queuing, requiring a second unit for consistent throughput. This limits its viability in team environments. Furthermore, during open-ended drafting, the model occasionally generates details not present in the source material. This behaviour, observed across multiple test runs, necessitates mandatory human review of all client-facing outputs. The risk of introducing unsupported claims cannot be mitigated by the hardware or its current software configuration. While the box achieves 92% accuracy in summarisation accuracy traps and 91% correct tool use, these strengths do not offset the core limitations in output quality and scalability. The cost of EUR 3,680, including Irish import VAT, reflects a significant investment for a system that cannot deliver on the fundamental requirement of producing sendable work without editorial intervention.

results.output: Owning its own AI hardware allows a small firm to process sensitive work without relying on external services. The machine delivers consistent performance across tasks, handling complex models at a steady rate—92 tokens per second for a mixture-of-experts architecture, and 28 times real time for transcription. This speed enables immediate turnaround on internal drafts, client summaries, and document preparation, all within the firm’s own network. The local model produces work that scores 3.00 on send-readiness, which means it is suitable for internal use but requires editing before external distribution. A comparison with a leading cloud-based model shows a clear gap in final quality, with the cloud model scoring 4.37. The firm’s own model performs well in accuracy tests, achieving 93 per cent on summarisation challenges, and correctly selects tools in 91 per cent of cases, with no errors in execution. Fine-tuning was completed entirely on the device, using just 25 to 100 examples. The tone improved slightly, but the gains were small and fell within normal variation. The model did not close the gap in document quality, nor did it eliminate the need for human oversight. The hardware supports only one user at full speed. If multiple people need to run tasks simultaneously, performance degrades or queues form. The model occasionally generates details not present in the source, a risk that cannot be removed by training. This means every client-facing output must be reviewed by a person before release. The investment is justified for privacy, speed, and control—but not for replacing editorial work.
